Abstract space and time demonstrate how generality can arise without spontaneous simple content: imagination varies instances while retaining a recurrent disposition or succession.
The expansion of causal association into power and government shows that ideational relations can organize social complexes by converting possible action into associative proximity.
Impression-audit and effect-oriented inquiry combine into a restricted science of mind that maps sources, operations, and consequences without postulating inaccessible substrates.
The cluster produces a relational ontology in which many apparent mental objects are reclassified as organized configurations of more elementary content.
The subject becomes a differential operator rather than an origin: it retains, weakens, separates, recombines, follows tendencies, and selectively generalizes impression-derived materials.
Temporality is generated through perceptible succession, conserved through memory, routed through customary association, and rearranged through imagination without becoming an empty medium.
Novelty becomes finite and grammatical: new complexes arise through transformations of relation and order rather than through creation of new simple elements.
Epistemic legitimacy is jointly genetic and operational: an idea must possess an impression-source and must not be applied beyond the structure that source can represent.
Causal explanation acquires political reach when powers of possible production are treated as sufficient to associate authority, duty, government, and obedience.
Methodologically, the system substitutes source-tracing, compositional analysis, and observable effects for unrestricted speculation about hidden essences.
Reality is thinkable only as content-bearing order: relations may vary, weaken, or generalize, but no positive spatial, temporal, or ideational structure survives complete removal of its terms.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Impression → idea → genealogical audit → permissible operation → renewed audit forms the basic recursive loop governing both composition and application.
Impression → memory recurrence → imaginative release → associative rerouting → stable complex converts experienced order into a reproducible but nonnecessary pattern.
Difference → distinction → separation → recombination → recurrent complex → demand for association transforms a logical test into a generative mental machine.
Sensory succession → custom → associative expectation → repeated transition recursively reinforces temporal contiguity as an imaginative pathway.
Order is the principal attractor: it returns as original position, changed conjunction, associative sequence, spatial disposition, temporal succession, and abstract invariant.
Causation follows an escalation path from ideational transition to actual production, possible exertion, interpersonal influence, and institutional hierarchy.
Particular configuration → selective regard → general term → heterogeneous applications → renewed particular representation forms the abstraction loop.
Absence of a distinct impression → non-distinguishability → non-separability → reclassification as manner of appearance is the cluster’s principal eliminative loop.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Impression-field supplies simple sensible and reflective materials; no subsequent operation adds unprecedented elemental content.
Impression-material recurs as ideas differentiated by retained force and fidelity: strong ordered recurrence produces memory, diminished recurrence opens imagination.
Distinguishable components become separable; separable components become recombinable; recombination produces unexperienced complexes.
Recurrent regularity among free combinations generates the requirement for a bond weaker than necessity and stronger than chance.
Resemblance, contiguity, and causation route ideational transitions through direct and progressively attenuated relational chains.
Associative routing stabilizes simple ideas into complex objects of thought while preserving the possibility of divergent recombination.
Analysis of order reveals spatial coexistence and temporal succession as arrangements of content rather than independent receptacles.
Selective recurrence of disposition or succession permits abstract representation without generating a contentless universal.
Genealogical testing excludes empty space, bare duration, changeless time, and other applications that outrun possible originating impressions.
The machine terminates in content-filled minima and experimentally established original tendencies rather than metaphysically disclosed ultimate causes.
Impression-given content → copied elemental ideas.
Copied recurrence → differentiation by vivacity and fidelity → memory/imagination bifurcation.
Imaginative release → separation and recombination → novel but derivative complexes.
Free combination → recurrent uniformity → rejection of chance → gentle associative regulation.
Associative regulation → relational chains → causal expansion → stabilized complex thought and social power.
Analysis of relation and order → coexistence/succession distinction → reconstruction of space and time as content-arrangements.
Impression genealogy → separability test → exclusion of empty forms and unsupported predications → content-filled conceptual closure.
Ideas cease to form a homogeneous class of copies and become differentiated by force, fidelity, compositional role, associative position, and representative function.
Provenance and operation become separable dimensions: common impression-derived materials can be archived, recombined, associated, or abstractly deployed.
Order becomes a productive object rather than a passive background, spanning mnemonic conservation, imaginative transposition, associative transition, and spatiotemporal constitution.
The opposition between freedom and determination collapses into bounded liberty governed by recurrent but defeasible tendencies.
Space and time are removed from the category of independent containers and relocated within the ordered appearance of positive contents.
Fiction is reclassified by operation: recombined complexes remain conceivable, while contentless forms and genealogically unsupported applications do not.
Causation becomes a cross-domain operator connecting natural production, possible action, mental transition, and institutional authority.
Philosophical method is redrawn around impression-audit, operational decomposition, and experimentally observable effects rather than unrestricted metaphysical postulation.
[Surface] The explicit objects are memory, imagination, ideational association, extension, duration, abstraction, and the formation of complex ideas.
[Structural] The active mechanisms are copying, recurrence, vivacity loss, order preservation, separation, recombination, associative routing, abstraction, and decomposition.
[Metastrategic] Conceptual disputes are reframed as questions of source, operation, relational distance, and permissible application rather than contests among untested metaphysical entities.

[Ontological / Temporal] Reality available to thought consists of content-bearing configurations, while time emerges from perceptible noncoexistence and is preserved or rearranged through mental recurrence.

[Methodological / Performative] The system repeatedly performs its own claim by decomposing apparent unities, tracing their sources, removing unsupported additions, and reconstructing them as relational operations.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The exact-copy principle strains against abstraction, which suppresses determinate sensible peculiarities while requiring a particular sensible representative.
Universal separability of simple ideas conflicts with the insistence that spatiality cannot be separated from all sensible quality and temporality cannot be separated from every succession.
Memory’s fidelity criterion presupposes access to an original arrangement whose independent recovery the system does not explain.
Vivacity and relational fidelity can classify the same recurrence differently, yet mixed cases are not formally resolved.
Imagination is described as freely combinatorial and universally guided by association, but the strength and defeasibility of that guidance remain unquantified.
Association is treated as an original quality, while contiguity is explained through acquired custom; the relation between innate principle and acquired pathway remains unresolved.
Causation receives maximal associative force before its nature is analyzed, and its extension into duty and authority compresses normative relations into productive power.
The inference from an idea’s perceptual genealogy to the impossibility or illegitimacy of independent existence exceeds what a theory of conception alone securely establishes.
Experienced duration varies with perceptual rate, but the relation between variable experienced time and objective succession remains underdetermined.
Order mutates from a standard against which recurrence is judged into a generative operator and then into the constitutive structure of spatial and temporal ideas.
Separability mutates from a positive authorization of imaginative freedom into a negative criterion for denying independent space and time.
Relation mutates from preserved or altered conjunction into a graded force capable of producing recall, complex thought, and social hierarchy.
Fiction mutates from lawful recombination into genealogical excess when an idea is predicated where no corresponding perceptual order can occur.
Causation mutates from one associative transition among ideas into a generalized schema of actual production, latent capacity, and institutional command.
Abstraction mutates copying from literal reproduction into selective representation while retaining dependence on determinate particular content.

Reality appears as a field of content-filled points and events whose coexistences, successions, similarities, and productive relations generate the structures ordinarily mistaken for independent forms.
The mind is an archive-workshop-network: memory preserves routes, imagination cuts and recombines components, and association weights the available transitions.
The subject is not a sovereign producer but a switching point through which impression-derived materials acquire differential force, order, and relational direction.
Time is a pulse of distinguishable succession rather than an empty stream; memory binds its experienced sequence, while imagination and association reroute its components.
The remaining freedom is navigational: the system permits movement among copied contents and weighted relations but no escape into contentless form or absolute spontaneity.
The extracted axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the cluster if the distinction between elemental provenance and relational organization remains primary.
Reconstruction is strongest where copy-dependence, separability, nonnecessary association, and content-bearing order jointly explain bounded mental productivity.

The system remains underdetermined at its thresholds and taxonomic closures: mnemonic vivacity, the exhaustiveness of associative relations, and the limits of separation are asserted rather than fully derived.
Coherence depends on recursive sequencing: imaginative freedom must precede associative regulation, and relational analysis must precede the rejection of independent space and time.
The architecture depends on productive omission at two terminal points: the unknown origin of associative attraction and the unverified phenomenology of sensible or successive minima.

No indispensable propositional element resists reduction, but the system’s actual movement is preserved only if order is allowed to mutate from remembered relation into associative machine and spatiotemporal form.

identity.kicker: Cluster · A Treatise of Human Nature
identity.title: Chapters 04–06
identity.context: Sect. III. Of The Ideas Of The Memory And Imagination · Sect. IV. Of The Connexion Or Association Of Ideas · Sect. III. Of The Other Qualities Of Our Idea Of Space And Time

items.text: The governing problem is how factual assent and practical reality can exceed bare conception when existence contributes no additional idea and positive conception remains bounded by perceptions.
The core thesis is that actuality is not represented by added content; belief differentiates an otherwise invariant object-idea through its forceful, steady, impression-related manner of conception.
A present impression and customary relation generate this manner by transferring vivacity to an absent, future, or otherwise merely conceived object.
The argument begins as an eliminative genealogy of existential content and becomes a reconstructive naturalistic psychology of assent, motivation, and affect.
Its movement is cumulative and recursive: ontological de-addition produces a modal theory of belief, which expands into a distributed economy of mental force.
Poetry, eloquence, passion, and madness then reverse the evidential direction by showing that apparent vivacity can imitate belief without supplying its settled authority.
Closure is operational rather than metaphysical: the system explains how ideas acquire reality-effects while withholding positive comprehension of mind-independent actuality.
The terminal correction appeals to causal provenance, steadiness, reflection, and general rules, but leaves their authority and relation to external reality incompletely grounded.
[Persistent] Positive conceptual content is restricted to impressions, ideas, and their copied or recombined perceptual materials.
[Persistent] Existence is not an additional quality, predicate, or idea but is identical with the object as conceived.
[Emergent] Bare conception, existential conception, and factual belief can preserve identical representational content while producing radically different cognitive and practical effects.
[Mutating] Belief begins as a difference in manner, becomes an intensification of force and vivacity, and terminates as a comparatively steady, impression-related, causally regulated mode.
[Persistent] Since contrary matters of fact remain conceivable, factual selection cannot arise from demonstrative necessity and must be determined by custom or association.
[Emergent] A present impression functions both as the experiential anchor of inference and as the reservoir from which vivacity is transmitted to a related idea.
[Emergent] Selective vivification gives absent and future objects present motivational efficacy without granting equivalent efficacy to every passing fiction.
[Mutating] Force and vivacity expand from a distinction between impressions and ideas into a transmissible causal currency linking belief, passion, imagination, and action.
[Emergent] Judgment, imagination, passion, and volition form a reciprocally permeable system rather than independent faculties.
[Attractor] Factuality converges on stable practical presence: an idea counts as real for the mind by persistently affecting inference, passion, and conduct without acquiring new content.
[Terminal] First-order vividness cannot authenticate itself; settled conviction requires discrimination by source, steadiness, reality-connection, reflection, and general rules.
[Attractor] Reality is retained as a regulative relation organizing assent and correction while its intrinsic extra-perceptual nature remains positively unrepresented.
Stable identity: the non-addition of existence persists unchanged from the analysis of being into the analysis of belief.

Absorption: the original question concerning the idea of existence disappears as an independent inquiry after becoming the premise that forces belief into a modal rather than representational explanation.
Functional mutation: present perception changes from the maximal positively available instance of being into the anchor and force-source of factual inference.
Escalation: force and vivacity move from taxonomic differences between perceptions to the defining mode of belief and then to a trans-domain mechanism of psychological causation.
Domain migration: custom moves from selecting one conceivable factual alternative to transmitting vivacity and thereby generating motivation, passion, and action.
Displacement: externality shifts from an intrinsically unfilled relative correlate to the “connection with reality” invoked when reflection regulates assent.
Reversal: vivacity initially explains why belief exceeds fiction, but counterfeit vivacity later demonstrates that intensity alone cannot establish genuine conviction.
Terminal transformation: the fact–fiction distinction moves from presumed content difference to scalar force difference and finally to causal pedigree, steadiness, and second-order correction.
Disappearance through absorption: conception, judgment, and reasoning cease to function as irreducible faculties once they have been recoded as modes and transitions within one conception-system.
The intrinsic nature of external objects remains a local ontological boundary; at cluster level, its scalable function is to deny any content-internal marker of actuality.
Poetry and madness remain local cases in subject matter but scale upward as indispensable stress tests of the proposed identity between belief and vivacity.
The proposition that existence adds no idea scales directly because it organizes both the boundary of ontology and the reconstruction of factual assent.
The present-impression requirement bridges conceptual genealogy and causal psychology by converting perceptual presence into a mechanism for generating belief.
The motivational dilemma catalyzes the major transition from defining belief phenomenologically to demonstrating its systemic necessity for conduct.
The simple equation of belief with occurrent intensity is superseded by a distinction between accidental vehemence and settled, source-regulated conviction.
The impression–idea taxonomy survives, but its original binary form is recoded into a graded and dynamically transmissible economy of perceptual force.
Neither existence nor belief is an additional predicate, quality, or representational component attached to an object-idea.
No intrinsic semantic mark distinguishes an actual object from the same object merely conceived.
No positive representational passage gives direct comprehension of a specifically extra-perceptual kind of being.
Matter-of-fact assent is not demonstrative necessity, and disbelief is not failure to understand the rejected proposition.
Judgment, reasoning, passion, and imagination are not causally sealed faculties governed by irreducibly different operations.
First-order intensity, imaginative completeness, and rhetorical vehemence do not independently authenticate factual belief.
Fiction and fact cannot be separated by an impermeable boundary at the level of represented content or raw vivacity.
Viable motivation can arise neither from present impressions alone nor from the indiscriminate efficacy of every passing idea.
The system excludes any ontology in which actual existence alters the intrinsic representational constitution of an object.
It excludes direct representational realism: positive knowledge cannot cross from perceptual content to the intrinsic nature of a heterogeneous external realm.
It excludes a rationalist construction of the factual world in which necessary conceptual connection determines existential truth.
It excludes faculty psychology as a final explanation: judgment cannot be an independent act that stamps truth onto completed ideas.
It excludes a sovereign rational subject insulated from custom, bodily condition, affective feedback, repetition, and rhetoric.
It excludes introspective foundationalism because the immediate felt strength of a perception cannot guarantee its own epistemic legitimacy.
The governing absence is the positively knowable essence of mind-independent actuality: it must remain thinkable as a correlate while unavailable as represented content.
The unavailable possibility is an intrinsic sign by which an idea could announce that its object exists independently.
No exact threshold separates vivid imagination, counterfeit belief, probable assent, and settled conviction.
The terminal ungrounded condition is the authority of general rules that distinguish legitimate causal vivification from accidental or pathological force.
Since existence adds no idea but belief exceeds bare conception, the surplus of factual assent must be modal and intensive rather than representational.
Perceptual closure combined with present-impression anchoring makes factual commitment a relation generated within experience rather than direct cognition of an external object’s intrinsic being.
If identical content produces different degrees of assent and action, force and steadiness must function as causal variables independent of representational composition.
The same intensification that constitutes factual assent also gives an absent object practical efficacy; epistemic commitment and motivation therefore share one mechanism.
The appeal to “connection with reality” regulates belief by reference to a term whose extra-perceptual nature the system denies it can positively comprehend.
Poetry, eloquence, and madness force belief to mutate from raw intensity into intensity qualified by causal provenance, steadiness, and resistance to reflective correction.
Customary transfer from impression to idea and passionate transfer back to the object-idea form a self-amplifying loop capable of strengthening assent beyond its initial basis.
Because fictional and factual ideas can share content, a familiar or believed component can lend force to an entire fictional network without converting the network into settled belief.

The reduction of judgment and reasoning to modes of conception, combined with the permeability of passion and imagination, yields a unified dynamics of mental force rather than a hierarchy of faculties.

Custom is accepted as the causal generator of factual assent while education is rejected as a valid ground of assent; the system therefore distinguishes psychological genesis from epistemic warrant without fully formalizing that distinction.
The system separates ontological content from actuality-effects: nothing representational is added, yet intensified conception transforms inference, passion, persistence, and conduct.
Factual warrant becomes second-order and genealogical: assent must be evaluated by how vivacity was produced and regulated, not merely by how forcefully it is felt.
Temporality becomes a force-transfer structure in which a present perception confers present efficacy upon absent and future objects.
The subject becomes a relay within circulating intensities rather than an autonomous judge: impressions, habits, passions, bodily states, and rhetoric jointly modulate assent.
Pathological and aesthetic cases are theoretically privileged because they separate apparent intensity from legitimate belief and thereby expose hidden conditions of the ordinary mechanism.
The mechanism enabling action toward absent realities simultaneously exposes judgment to capture by repetition, eloquence, temperament, and affective feedback.
The cluster produces practical realism without positive metaphysical realism: ideas can govern life as realities even though independent actuality supplies no distinct conceptual content.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Negative recursion: existence adds no content → belief cannot add content → factual difference relocates to manner → manner requires an intensive mechanism.
Generative loop: present impression → customary transition → transferred vivacity → intensified related idea → belief → action and passion.
Affective feedback loop: belief excites passion → passion vivifies its object → the vivified object increases assent → strengthened assent reinforces passion.
Fictional diffusion loop: familiar anchor → relational spread of vivacity → easier imaginative reception → affective engagement without complete judgmental assent.
Counterfeit escalation: temperament, eloquence, or bodily ferment raises ideas toward impression-like force, culminating in the possible collapse of operative truth–falsehood discrimination.
Corrective loop: excessive vividness generates error → reflection identifies accidental provenance → general rules discount local force → graded conviction is restored.

Aporetic return: correction invokes reality-connection, but positive comprehension of external reality remains unavailable, returning epistemic regulation to the boundary established by perceptual closure.

The conceptual attractor is regulated vivacity: sufficient force to make ideas cognitively and practically present, sufficient steadiness to resist fluctuation, and sufficient pedigree to distinguish them from counterfeits.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Perceptual admissibility: every positive idea must derive from perceptual materials; no extra-perceptual existential content is available.
Representational invariance: content of object O = content of O-as-existent = content of believed O; therefore factual difference cannot be compositional.
Modal generation: present impression I + customary relation R(I,O) → transfer of vivacity → steady intensified conception of O → belief.
Operational expansion: belief in O → increased presence and persistence of O → influence on passion, imagination, and action.
Recursive amplification: passion or related vivid ideas → renewed vivacity in O → strengthened assent and affective efficacy.
Counterfeit production: non-customary vivification by rhetoric, temperament, or bodily ferment → belief-like force without secure factual pedigree.
Regulatory closure: source-reflection + general rules + reality-connection → correction of apparent intensity, while external actuality remains an intrinsically unfilled correlate.

Existential-origin test → elimination of added being-content → perceptual closure → belief-surplus problem → content invariance → relocation to manner → force-and-vivacity definition → customary transfer from present impression → practical and affective expansion → counterfeit vivification → correction by provenance and general rules → unresolved appeal to reality beyond positive representation.
Being is reclassified from a detachable predicate into the nondiscriminating status of conceived presentation.
The actual–possible distinction is relocated from represented content to the force, steadiness, provenance, and practical effects of conception.
The internal–external distinction is redrawn as a problem of mediation, relational attribution, and causal anchoring rather than qualitative content.
Understanding is reclassified from a hierarchy of faculties into a single conception-system differentiated by necessity, association, intensity, and transition.
Absent and future objects are reclassified as potentially present causes of conduct when belief supplies sufficient force.
Fact, fiction, persuasion, and madness become neighboring configurations within one economy rather than categorically separate mental domains.
Epistemic reading must become genealogical and second-order, tracking the source and regulation of vivacity rather than trusting represented content or felt intensity alone.
Surface level: the system addresses existence, external objects, belief, factual assent, motivation, passion, fiction, eloquence, and madness.
Structural level: impression-copy constraints, present-perception anchoring, customary association, force transmission, affective feedback, and corrective rules compose one distributed mechanism.
Metastrategic level: metaphysical and epistemic distinctions are converted into tests of perceptual origin, modal difference, causal provenance, and susceptibility to correction.
Ontological/Temporal level: being adds no essence, while absent and future objects acquire present causal efficacy through impression-related modes of conception.

Methodological/Performative level: the system first compresses distinctions into a scalar mechanism and then uses poetry and madness to force its own refinement from simple intensity to regulated intensity.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The system oscillates between existence as the universal status of every presented perception and existence as the actuality affirmed only in belief; the same term covers conceptual presence and factual commitment.
Perceptual closure denies positive access to extra-perceptual being, yet external objects are said to occasion perceptions and “reality-connection” regulates assent.
The scalar reduction of belief is strained by vivid fiction and poetry, which may exhibit greater apparent vehemence while remaining experientially and epistemically weaker.
General rules repair the insufficiency of first-order force but lack a specified origin, authority, and mechanism capable of avoiding circular dependence on already accepted beliefs.
Habit is necessary to generate factual assent, while education demonstrates that repeated habit can produce epistemically invalid assent; causal production and warrant remain incompletely separated.
Existence mutates from the explicit object of conceptual genealogy into a zero-addition constraint governing every subsequent account of belief.
Force and vivacity mutate from marks distinguishing impressions and ideas into transferable quantities linking cognition, affect, imagination, and action.
Belief mutates from intensified conception into regulated intensification once counterfeit cases show that occurrent vividness is insufficient.
Truth and reality mutate from presumed properties of represented objects into causal and regulatory terms governing easy reception, assent, and reflective correction.
Reality is implicitly modeled as a perceptually closed transmission machine in which impressions and ideas circulate, receive, lose, and redistribute force.
The subject is a relay and regulatory threshold within this machine, not its sovereign origin: habit, affect, bodily ferment, and reflection compete to set the force of ideas.
Time is organized around present anchors that draw absent and future objects into current causal efficacy through associative transmission.

The remaining struggle is navigational: distinguish customary and regulated reality-effects from rhetorical, passionate, poetic, or pathological counterfeits without access to an intrinsic sign of actuality.

The current-level axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the principal engine: existential non-addition → modal belief → customary vivification → practical expansion → counterfeit stress → regulatory correction.
What remains underdetermined is the exact dimensional structure of force and vivacity, the mechanism of their transfer, and the threshold separating belief from vivid imagination.
The architecture is coherent at the functional level but not metaphysically closed: it explains reality-effects more successfully than independent actuality or the warrant of correction.
Its strongest construction is the transition from representational invariance to a unified mechanism explaining assent, motivation, passion, imagination, and action.
Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if poetry, eloquence, and madness remain recursive tests that transform the initial scalar account rather than detachable illustrations.

The elements resistant to axiomatic reduction are the felt quality of belief, the positive nature of external actuality, and the authority of the general rules that arbitrate genuine and counterfeit force.
