items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo homo finitus, ex affectibus et causis externis compositus, libertatem communem et intellectualem acquirere possit sine imperio voluntatis aut exemptione a Natura.

Thesis globalis libertatem constituit ut amplificationem graduatam causalitatis propriae, quae servitutem affectivam per compositionem corporalem, civilem et cognitivam in beatitudinem activam transformat.
Argumentatio est apophatica et reconstructiva: falsas autonomiae, moralitatis et salutis formas excludit, deinde terminos negatos intra causalitatem immanentem denuo constituit.
Motus procedit a reductione affectuum ad servitutem, a servitute ad compositionem socialem potentiarum, atque ab hac compositione ad cognitionem intuitivam et Amorem intellectualem.
Progressio est cumulativa, recursiva, amplificativa et spiralis, quia quisque gradus causam efficaciae gradus sequentis producit et terminus ad operationem priorum retrovertitur.

Clausura non liberationem absolutam sed duplicem stabilitatem praebet: acquiescentiam finitam intra eventus necessarios et beatitudinem quae, ex fine apparente, in causam permanentem activitatis convertitur.
[Persistent] Natura ex necessitate immanenti agit; libertas igitur non causalitatem tollit, sed modum quo necessitas per rem finitam explicatur mutat.
[Persistent] Passio est determinatio corporalis et ideationalis cuius causa a subiecto tantum partialiter explicatur; actio crescit prout idea causae adaequatur.
[Mutating] Conatus transit ab essentia perseverandi ad virtutem rationalem, compositionem communem et actionem intellectualem beatificam, identitate directionis servata.
[Mutating] Libertas est gradus causalitatis adaequatae qui primum affectus ordinat, deinde condiciones corporales et civiles componit, postremo in stabilitatem intellectualem extenditur.
[Persistent] Cognitio efficax repraesentatio iners esse nequit: veritas tantum potentiam auget ubi affectum, corpus, institutionem aut ordinem imaginum causaliter immutat.
[Emergent] Finitas, quae causis externis servitutem exponit, eadem dependentia est ex qua compositio corporum, mutuum auxilium et potentia communis generantur.
[Mutating] Corpus ex sede affectionum in infrastructuram materialem libertatis et tandem in dispositionem positivam ad ampliorem actionem Mentis mutatur.
[Mutating] Ratio vim obtinet tantum cum ex norma intelligibili in affectum contrarium, cupiditatem activam, institutionem stabilem et transitum ad intuitionem convertitur.
[Mutating] Socialitas ab imitatione conflictiva ad Civitatem coercitivam et inde ad infrastructuram cooperationis rationalis progreditur, origine passionali numquam omnino deleta.
[Emergent] Bonum, malum, iustum et iniustum sunt instrumenta comparativa potentiae finitae; in libertate perfecta functionem terminaliter amittunt.
[Mutating] Necessitas ex signo dominationis externae in obiectum intellectus et formam ontologicam libertatis sapientis invertitur.
[Attractor] Intellegere, cognitio Dei, acquiescentia, intuitio, Amor intellectualis et beatitudo constituunt unum attractorem ascensionalem potentiae non-rivalis.
[Emergent] Tempus affectivum bifurcatur inter durationem imaginativam, quae praesentiam et intensitatem distribuit, et aeternitatem intelligibilem, quae successionem et memoriam non continuat.
[Terminal] Sapientis beatitudo non est praemium virtutis sed exercitium eius, quo positio terminalis in causam conservandae libertatis convertitur.

Lætitia et Tristitia identitatem directionalem servant, sed ex indicibus mutationis affectivae in criterios ethicos et tandem in differentiam inter laetitiam activam et fluctuationem passivam amplificantur.
Cupiditas ex affectu primitivo in essentiam conatus, cupiditatem rationalem et genealogiam actionis transit; obiectum eius causalitati originis subordinatur.
Veritas functionem mutat: ex auctoritate polemica fit vis affective condicionata, deinde technica corporalis et intellectualis transformationis.
Corpus ex correlato passionis in infrastructuram nutritionis et laboris, deinde in instrumentum ampliandae potentiae Mentis migrat.
Socialitas redit functione mutata: imaginatio alterius conflictum parit, Civitas eum coercet, cooperatio rationalis dependentiam in amplificationem convertit.
Libertas ab exclusione decreti indeterminati ad ecologiam materialiter sustentatam et tandem ad mutationem proportionis inter actionem et passionem transit.
Necessitas, initio negatio liberi decreti, in condicionem acquiescentiae et postremo in formam libertatis intellectualis absorbetur.
Vocabula moralia ab institutione affectiva ad comparationem rationalem migrant et, libertate perfecta approximata, opere navigationis peracto recedunt.
Dei cognitio ab attractore intellectionis ad acquiescentiam et Amorem intellectualem progreditur, dum amor reciprocus et anthropomorphicus invertitur in actionem reflexivam.
Imaginatio res absentes affective praesentat et rationem praeparat, sed in aeternitate memorativa operatione sua exhausta terminaliter evanescit.
Taxonomiae affectuum et casus actuum manent machinae locales; hoc gradu servantur tantum ut probationes legis qua causa, intensitas et totum potentiae valorem constituunt.
Differentiae temporales et concursus imaginum sursum amplificantur in doctrinam generalem de distributione praesentiae affectivae, sed nondum ipsae aeternitatem intelligibilem constituunt.
Aestimatio actuum singulorum absorbetur in genealogiam causae: eadem species exterior potest passionem, actionem rationalem aut virtutem exprimere.
Trias affectuum, doctrina affectus fortioris et relatio affectionum ad Deum unitates inferiores coniungunt, quia mutationem potentiae in transitum cognitivum convertunt.
Transitus praesentis gradus fit ubi cognitio desinit esse mera veritas et fit affectus activus, dispositio corporalis atque causa laetitiae intellectualis.
Civitas transitum maiorem efficit cum potestas coercitiva in iura, cooperationem materialem et causalitatem propriam civium convertitur.
Distinctio durationis et aeternitatis unitates superiores coniungit, dum aptitudo Corporis fit commissura inter praxim temporalem et cognitionem non successivam.
Moralitas tristitiae, inventarium affectuum et refutatio voluntatis fiunt secundaria, quia eorum opera negativa in machinam positivam cooperationis et beatitudinis absorbetur.
Libertas neque decretum indeterminatum neque imperium voluntatis est; nulla actio humana nexum causarum naturalium interrumpit.
Natura nec fines externos nec ordinem moralem transcendentem nec Deum voluntate mutabilem admittit.
Cognitio vera, si affectum et ordinem Corporis non mutat, passionem sola contradictione logica superare nequit.
Individuum sibi sufficiens excluditur, quia corpus, res externae, alii homines et Deus intra ipsam constitutionem potentiae agunt.
Utilitas propria et commune bonum non sunt contraria, nisi conatus sub imaginatione competitiva et causalitate inadaequata consideretur.
Civitas et libertas non sunt oppositiones absolutae; discrimen verum est inter administrationem metus et productionem potentiae communis.
Corpus non est adversarius Mentis aut aeternitatis, sed condicio sine qua affectus ordinari et intellectus amplificari nequeunt.
Aeternitas non est continuatio memoriae personalis, neque virtus ex spe praemii, metu poenae aut iudicio post mortem pendet.
Falsum esse oportet Naturam a legislatore finali vel Deo personali ordinari, quia omnis norma valida ex relationibus immanentibus potentiae generatur.
Falsum esse oportet mentem abstractam sine affectu et corpore veritatem inertem in imperium practicum convertere posse.
Falsum esse oportet subiectum esse substantiam clausam aut extra Deum subsistere, quia libertas ex relationibus adaequate compositis nascitur.
Falsum esse oportet speciem externam actus valorem eius continere; passio et actio discernuntur ex modo causationis, non ex similitudine operis.
Falsum esse oportet coactionem securitatemque per se cooperationem rationalem producere; communitas actualis mediationes affectivas, iuridicas et materiales postulat.
Falsum esse oportet aeternam Mentis identitatem cum historia memorativa personae coincidere aut mensura temporali definiri posse.
Ontologice inadmissibilis est locus exterior Naturae ex quo subiectum finitum causas totius sine participatione contemplaretur.
Systema circum absentiam conversionis instantaneae veritatis in potentiam ordinatur; nulla claritas minima per se transmutationem passionis praestat.
Impossibilis est status hominis finiti omni passione, corpore, societate et causa externa absolute liberati.
Absentia iudicis remunerantis et Dei affective reciproci cogit virtutem causam immanentem atque sufficientem sui ipsius fieri.
Systema circum pontem incompletum inter passionem actualem et libertatem perfectam laborat: affectus rationalis, Civitas cooperativa et experientia aeternitatis causaliter nondum plene nectuntur.
Libertas est ecologia potentiae, quia asymmetria causarum externarum tantum per relationem corporalis aptitudinis, cooperationis socialis et intelligentiae adaequatae convertitur.
Veritas vim practicam obtinet cum fit affectus contrarius, cupiditas activa, dispositio institutionalis et laetitia ex cognitione adaequata.
Conatus propriae conservationis structuram non-rivalem acquirit, quia auxilium commune et aliena beatitudo potentiam singularis minuere non debent sed augere possunt.
Corpus est simul terminus partis memorativae pereuntis et medium materiale quo cognitio, libertas et maior participatio actionis intellectualis producuntur.
Necessitas vim inversivam exercet: eadem causalitas quae libertatem arbitrii negat campum immanentem constituit in quo causalitas propria et libertas sapientis crescunt.
Civitas est convertor inter servitutem et libertatem, non terminus liberationis: vim externam in cooperationem mutat, dum Ratio transitum ad actionem intellectualem aperit.
Categoriae boni et mali necessariae sunt dum potentia finita navigat, sed attractore beatitudinis approximato recedunt, quia beatitudo iam non merces sed virtus est.
Tempus ethicorum operum duplicem rationem habet: praesentia imaginativa intensitates distribuit, Ratio utilitates trans durationem ordinat, aeternitas autem successionem omnino suspendit.
Beatitudo totam seriem retroactive ordinat, quia finis apparens in machinam fit quae intellectum auget, passiones minuit et propriam praesentiam conservat.
Subiectum est proportio multiscalaris causalitatum partialium, relationum socialium et idearum adaequatarum, cuius identitas ex potentia agendi potius quam clausura substantialis constat.
Ontologia fit ecologia multiscalaris potentiae, in qua corpora, affectus, institutiones et ideae sunt modi distribuendi causalitatem immanentem.
Libertas neque proprietas individui neque status politicus solus est, sed relatio distributa qua corpus, societas et intellectus causam actionis sufficientius exprimunt.
Epistemologia obtinet statum technologiae causalis, quia cognitio vera affectus, ordinem Corporis et facultatem ulterius cognoscendi simul producit.
Politica fit distributio condicionum causalitatis propriae, cuius mensura est utrum communicatio boni potentiam singularem et communem simul amplificet.
Tempus non est unum medium continuum: affectus inhabitant topologiam praesentiae, deliberatio seriem utilitatum, intellectus autem essentiam non durationalem.
Theologia in ontologiam reflexivam convertitur, quia Deus obiectum supremum manet sine persona affective reciproca, iar Amor intellectualis fit explicatio immanentis sui cognitionis.
Ethica est navigatio finitudinis quae ordinat potentiam donec instrumenta comparativa boni et mali in virtute beatifica propriam necessitatem amittant.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Causa externa passionem auget, potentiam propriam minuit et ignorantiam causae stabilit; ignorantia autem rem externam iterum quasi dominam affectus figit.
Affectus contrarius ordinationem incipit, ordinatio actionem auget, actio claritatem causae firmat, et claritas ulteriorem passivitatem minuit.
Convenientia rationalis potentias componit, cooperatio potentiam singularis auget, et potentia aucta maiorem cooperationem rationalem efficit.
Conflictus ad coercitionem, coercitio ad securitatem, securitas ad cooperationem tendit; circuitus tamen regreditur si metus fundamentum solum institutionis manet.
Oeconomia Corporis libertatem cognitionis sustinet, cognitio aptitudinem actionis auget, et Corpus ad plures actiones aptum novam cognitionem recipit.
Cognitio et libertas circuitum positivum efficiunt: Ratio cupiditatem intuitionis parit, intuitio laetitiam auget, et laetitia ulteriorem intelligentiam sustentat.
Communicatio boni non-rivalis Amorem auget, auctus Amor participationem aliorum desiderat, et participatio potentiam communem iterum amplificat.
Beatitudo est attractor terminalis et circuitus sui conservativus: quo magis adest, eo plus Mens intelligit et minus ab affectibus externis regitur.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessitas immanens + potentia finita → campus relationum in quo omnis res agit quatenus causas suas exprimit et patitur quatenus ab externis exceditur.
Mutatio Corporis + idea inadaequata → affectus passivus + causalitas partialis + attribuenda vis causae externae.
Causa externa superior → imminutio potentiae → maior receptivitas passionis → servitus affectiva se ipsam amplificans.
Conatus + affectus contrarius fortior + cupiditas activa → initium causalitatis propriae sine interruptione necessitatis.
Convenientia rationalis + auxilia communia + condiciones materiales → compositio socialis potentiarum → maior aptitudo corporis et intellectus.
Intellectus necessitatis + ordinatio affectuum + causalitas adaequata → libertas relativa ut participatio intelligibilis nexus causarum.
Ratio adaequata → cupiditas cognitionis tertii generis → intuitio essentiae singularis → Amor intellectualis.
Cognitio intuitiva + laetitia activa + Amor intellectualis → beatitudo → augmentum intellectus → stabilitas libertatis sub necessitate.
Pluralitas affectuum → reductio ad mutationes potentiae → asymmetria causalium virium → servitus → affectus rationalis → compositio communis → intelligentia adaequata → beatitudo activa.
Conflictus imaginativus → Civitas coercitiva → securitas → iura et cooperatio → causalitas propria civium → acquiescentia sub necessitate.
Corpus affectum et durans → aptitudo materialiter aucta → ordinatio imaginum → plures actiones → cognitio intuitiva → maior proportio Mentis sub aeternitate intellecta.
Psychologia affectuum in ecologiam potentiae reordinatur, ubi corpora, institutiones et ideae non regiones separatae sed modi unius distributionis causalis sunt.
Moralitas actuum exteriorum corruit; valor transfertur ad modum causationis, effectum in potentiam totius et originem affectivam vel intellectualem.
Corpus et oeconomia ex adiunctis ethicae in condiciones constitutivas cognitionis, libertatis et dispositionis rationalis transferuntur.
Oppositio inter Civitatem et libertatem reponitur oppositione inter regimen metus et ordinem qui proportionem actionis ad passionem collective mutat.
Necessitas reclassificatur ab externo limite agentiae in campum immanentem autonomiae relationalis et intelligentiae causalium nexuum.
Deus et aeternitas a personis vel continuationibus temporalibus transferuntur ad structuram reflexivam causalitatis immanentis et conceptionem essentiae sub necessitate.
Lectio systematis debet functiones mutantes terminorum sequi, quia actus, affectus, Corpus, libertas et beatitudo identitatem nominalem servant dum statum structuralem mutant.
In gradu superficiei systema nomina affectuum, utilitates, leges, corpus, mortem et beatitudinem tractat ut quaestiones vitae humanae sub servitute et libertate.
In gradu structurali casus omnes per mutationes corporis, causalitatem partialem, mediationem socialem et ordinem idearum distribuuntur.
In gradu metastrategico moderatio a condemnatione passionum ad productionem affectuum activorum, cooperationis et laetitiae cognitivae transfertur.
In gradu ontologico et temporali subiectum est pars Naturae necessario determinata, cuius duratio imaginativa ab aeternitate intelligibili distinguitur.
In gradu methodologico et performativo demonstratio reductionem, reclassificationem et mutationem quam describit ipsa exercet, donec negatio in circuitum positivum beatitudinis convertatur.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Veritas imperium automaticum non habet, sed libertas terminalis ab intelligentia pendet; quantitas et forma cognitionis quae vim affectivam sufficientem producit indeterminatae manent.
Concordia rationalis necessaria dicitur, sed Civitas minis fundata cooperationem rationalem ex sola securitate deducere nequit.
Corpus est temporale et pars structurae Mentis pereuntis, sed eius aptitudo maiorem participationem aeternitatis producere dicitur sine mechanismi proportionis plena demonstratione.
Negatio finalitatis cum attractore Dei cognitionis et beatitudinis cohaeret tantum si attractor causa immanens, non finis Naturae praestitutus, intelligitur.
Virtus ab cognitione aeternitatis independens manet, quamvis figura summa sapientis per intellectum aeternum et Amorem intellectualem definiatur.
Amor intellectualis aeternus sine principio ponitur, sed accessus ad cognitionem intuitivam progressionis gradatim acquisitae forma narratur.
Cupiditas punctum mutationis constituit ubi ex affectu primitivo in essentiam actualem, cupiditatem activam et principium cognitionis altioris transit.
Civitas functionem mutat ubi ex exteriori coercitione in convertorem securitatis, cooperationis et causalitatis propriae civium transit.
Corpus functionem mutat ubi ex sede durationis et passionis fit dispositio positiva ad actionem, cognitionem et aeternitatem intelligibilem.
Necessitas sensum mutat ubi ex indice excessus externi fit obiectum acquiescentiae et forma libertatis sapientis.
Beatitudo statum terminalem amittit ubi ex fine disciplinae in ipsam virtutem et causam minuendarum passionum invertitur.
Realitas implicite est rete virium finitarum, corporum, institutionum et idearum, in quo causalitas perpetuo distribuitur, componitur aut captatur.
Subiectum est nodus permeabilis, corporaliter et socialiter compositus, qui liber fit quatenus nexus determinantes clarius per ipsum exprimuntur.
Tempus est topologia bifurcata: duratio praesentiam, memoriam et passionem distribuit, aeternitas autem essentiam sine successione aut recordatione exhibet.
Navigatio possibilis est spiralis conversio canalium causalium: conflictus in cooperationem, fixatio externa in intelligentiam et mortalitatis metus in beatitudinem praesentem transferuntur.
Axiomata necessitatis, affectus, conatus, compositionis socialis, aptitudinis Corporis et intelligentiae sufficiunt ad machinam minimam huius gradus restituendam.
Nondum satis determinantur productio affectus rationalis fortioris, conversio Civitatis coercitivae et relatio experientiae aeternitatis ad Mentem memoriam amittentem.
Structura firmissima est circuitus qui conatum, cooperationem, ideam adaequatam, intellectum necessitatis et auctam potentiam cognoscendi connectit.
Restitutio verum motum servat si libertatem ut amplificationem recursivam potentiae et remedia temporalia ut dispositionem ad cognitionem intuitivam exhibet, non ut liberationem instantaneam.
Systema hoc gradu cohaeret per reditum terminorum cum mutatione functionis, sed nexus inter demonstrationem, experientiam aeternitatis et vim imaginis sapientis reductioni plenae resistit.
The system asks how a finite human being, composed of affects and external causes, can acquire common and intellectual freedom without dominion of the will or exemption from Nature.

The global thesis establishes freedom as the graduated amplification of one's own causality, which transforms affective servitude into active blessedness through bodily, civil, and cognitive composition.
The argument is apophatic and reconstructive: it excludes false forms of autonomy, morality, and salvation, then reconstitutes the negated terms within immanent causality.
The movement proceeds from the reduction of affects to servitude, from servitude to the social composition of powers, and from this composition to intuitive knowledge and intellectual Love.

The progression is cumulative, recursive, amplificatory, and spiral, because each stage produces the cause of the efficacy of the following stage and the terminus turns back to the operation of the preceding ones.

The closure offers not absolute liberation but a twofold stability: finite acquiescence within necessary events and blessedness which, from an apparent end, is converted into a permanent cause of activity.
[Persistent] Nature acts from immanent necessity; freedom therefore does not remove causality, but changes the mode in which necessity is explicated through a finite thing.
[Persistent] Passion is a bodily and ideational determination whose cause is explained by the subject only partially; action increases insofar as the idea of the cause is adequate.
[Mutating] Conatus passes from the essence of persevering to rational virtue, common composition, and blessed intellectual action, with directional identity preserved.
[Mutating] Freedom is a degree of adequate causality that first orders the affects, then composes bodily and civil conditions, and finally extends into intellectual stability.
[Persistent] Effective knowledge cannot be inert representation: truth increases power only where it causally changes an affect, body, institution, or order of images.
[Emergent] Finitude, which exposes one to servitude under external causes, is the same dependence from which the composition of bodies, mutual aid, and common power are generated.
[Mutating] The Body is transformed from the seat of affections into the material infrastructure of freedom and finally into a positive disposition toward the greater action of the Mind.
[Mutating] Reason obtains force only when it is converted from an intelligible norm into a contrary affect, active desire, stable institution, and transition to intuition.
[Mutating] Sociality progresses from conflictual imitation to the coercive State and thence to the infrastructure of rational cooperation, its passional origin never wholly erased.
[Emergent] Good, evil, just, and unjust are comparative instruments of finite power; in perfect freedom they ultimately lose their function.
[Mutating] Necessity is inverted from a sign of external domination into an object of intellect and the ontological form of the freedom of the wise.
[Attractor] Understanding, knowledge of God, acquiescence, intuition, intellectual Love, and blessedness constitute one ascending attractor of non-rivalrous power.
[Emergent] Affective time bifurcates between imaginative duration, which distributes presence and intensity, and intelligible eternity, which does not continue succession and memory.
[Terminal] The blessedness of the wise is not the reward of virtue but its exercise, whereby a terminal position is converted into a cause of preserving freedom.
Joy and Sadness preserve directional identity, but are amplified from indicators of affective change into ethical criteria and finally into the difference between active joy and passive fluctuation.
Desire passes from primitive affect into the essence of conatus, rational desire, and the genealogy of action; its object is subordinated to the causality of its origin.
Truth changes function: from polemical authority it becomes affectively conditioned force, then a technique of bodily and intellectual transformation.
The Body migrates from the correlate of passion to the infrastructure of nourishment and labor, then to an instrument for amplifying the power of the Mind.
Sociality returns with altered function: imagination of another produces conflict, the State restrains it, rational cooperation converts dependence into amplification.
Freedom passes from the exclusion of an indeterminate decree to a materially sustained ecology and finally to a change in the proportion between action and passion.
Necessity, initially the negation of free decree, is absorbed into the condition of acquiescence and finally into the form of intellectual freedom.
Moral terms migrate from affective institution to rational comparison and, with perfect freedom approximated, withdraw once their work of navigation is completed.
Knowledge of God progresses from an attractor of understanding to acquiescence and intellectual Love, while reciprocal and anthropomorphic love is inverted into reflexive action.
Imagination affectively presents absent things and prepares reason, but in memorial eternity it ultimately vanishes, its operation exhausted.
Taxonomies of affects and cases of acts remain local machines; at this level they are preserved only as proofs of the law by which cause, intensity, and the whole of power constitute value.
Temporal differences and the concurrence of images are amplified upward into a general doctrine of the distribution of affective presence, but do not yet themselves constitute intelligible eternity.
The evaluation of individual acts is absorbed into the genealogy of cause: the same outward species can express passion, rational action, or virtue.
The triad of affects, the doctrine of the stronger affect, and the relation of affections to God join the lower units, because they convert a change of power into a cognitive transition.
The transition of the present level occurs where knowledge ceases to be mere truth and becomes an active affect, bodily disposition, and cause of intellectual joy.
The State effects the greater transition when coercive power is converted into rights, material cooperation, and the citizens' own causality.
The distinction between duration and eternity joins the higher units, while the aptitude of the Body becomes the joint between temporal praxis and non-successive knowledge.
The morality of sadness, the inventory of affects, and the refutation of the will become secondary, because their negative work is absorbed into the positive machine of cooperation and blessedness.
Freedom is neither an indeterminate decree nor dominion of the will; no human action interrupts the nexus of natural causes.
Nature admits neither external ends nor a transcendent moral order nor a God mutable by will.
True knowledge, if it does not change affect and the order of the Body, cannot overcome passion by logical contradiction alone.
The self-sufficient individual is excluded, because body, external things, other humans, and God act within the very constitution of power.
Self-interest and the common good are not contrary, unless conatus is considered under competitive imagination and inadequate causality.
The State and freedom are not absolute oppositions; the true distinction is between the administration of fear and the production of common power.
The Body is not the adversary of the Mind or of eternity, but the condition without which affects cannot be ordered and intellect cannot be amplified.
Eternity is not the continuation of personal memory, nor does virtue depend on hope of reward, fear of punishment, or judgment after death.
It must be false that Nature is ordered by a final legislator or personal God, because every valid norm is generated from immanent relations of power.
It must be false that an abstract mind without affect and body can convert inert truth into practical dominion.
It must be false that the subject is a closed substance or subsists outside God, because freedom is born from adequately composed relations.
It must be false that the external appearance of an act contains its value; passion and action are distinguished by the mode of causation, not by similarity of work.
It must be false that coercion and security in themselves produce rational cooperation; actual community requires affective, juridical, and material mediations.
It must be false that the eternal identity of the Mind coincides with the memorial history of the person or can be defined by temporal measure.
An external place outside Nature is ontologically inadmissible, from which a finite subject might contemplate the causes of the whole without participation.
The system is ordered around the absence of an instantaneous conversion of truth into power; no minimal clarity by itself secures the transmutation of passion.
A state of finite humanity absolutely liberated from every passion, body, society, and external cause is impossible.
The absence of a rewarding judge and an affectively reciprocal God compels virtue to become the immanent and sufficient cause of itself.
The system labors around an incomplete bridge between actual passion and perfect freedom: rational affect, the cooperative State, and the experience of eternity are not yet fully causally connected.
Freedom is an ecology of power, because the asymmetry of external causes is converted only through the relation of bodily aptitude, social cooperation, and adequate intelligence.
Truth obtains practical force when it becomes a contrary affect, active desire, institutional disposition, and joy from adequate knowledge.
The conatus of self-preservation acquires a non-rivalrous structure, because common aid and another's blessedness need not diminish but can increase an individual's power.
The Body is at once the terminus of the perishing memorial part and the material medium through which knowledge, freedom, and greater participation in intellectual action are produced.
Necessity exercises an inversive force: the same causality that denies freedom of choice constitutes the immanent field in which one's own causality and the freedom of the wise increase.
The State is a converter between servitude and freedom, not the terminus of liberation: it changes external force into cooperation, while Reason opens the transition to intellectual action.
The categories of good and evil are necessary while finite power navigates, but withdraw as the attractor of blessedness is approached, because blessedness is no longer a reward but virtue.
The time of ethical works has a double account: imaginative presence distributes intensities, Reason orders utilities across duration, but eternity wholly suspends succession.
Blessedness retroactively orders the entire series, because the apparent end becomes a machine that increases intellect, diminishes passions, and preserves its own presence.
The subject is a multiscalar proportion of partial causalities, social relations, and adequate ideas, whose identity consists in power of acting rather than substantial closure.
Ontology becomes a multiscalar ecology of power, in which bodies, affects, institutions, and ideas are modes of distributing immanent causality.
Freedom is neither a property of the individual nor political status alone, but a distributed relation by which body, society, and intellect more sufficiently express the cause of action.
Epistemology acquires the status of causal technology, because true knowledge simultaneously produces affects, the order of the Body, and the capacity for further knowing.
Politics becomes the distribution of conditions of one's own causality, whose measure is whether the communication of good simultaneously amplifies individual and common power.
Time is not one continuous medium: affects inhabit a topology of presence, deliberation a series of utilities, but intellect non-durational essence.

Theology is converted into reflexive ontology, because God remains the supreme object without an affectively reciprocal person, and intellectual Love becomes the explication of immanent self-knowledge.
Ethics is the navigation of finitude that orders power until the comparative instruments of good and evil lose their own necessity in blessed virtue.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: An external cause increases passion, diminishes one's own power, and stabilizes ignorance of the cause; ignorance in turn fixes the external thing again as though mistress of affect.
A contrary affect begins ordering, ordering increases action, action strengthens clarity of cause, and clarity diminishes further passivity.
Rational agreement composes powers, cooperation increases individual power, and increased power produces greater rational cooperation.
Conflict tends toward coercion, coercion toward security, security toward cooperation; yet the circuit regresses if fear remains the sole foundation of institution.
The economy of the Body sustains freedom of knowledge, knowledge increases aptitude for action, and a Body suited to more actions receives new knowledge.
Knowledge and freedom produce a positive circuit: Reason generates desire for intuition, intuition increases joy, and joy sustains further intelligence.
The communication of non-rivalrous good increases Love, increased Love desires the participation of others, and participation again amplifies common power.
Blessedness is a terminal attractor and self-preserving circuit: the more it is present, the more the Mind understands and the less it is governed by external affects.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Immanent necessity + finite power → a field of relations in which every thing acts insofar as it expresses its causes and suffers insofar as it is exceeded by externals.
Change of the Body + inadequate idea → passive affect + partial causality + force attributed to an external cause.
Superior external cause → diminution of power → greater receptivity to passion → self-amplifying affective servitude.
Conatus + stronger contrary affect + active desire → beginning of one's own causality without interruption of necessity.
Rational agreement + common aids + material conditions → social composition of powers → greater aptitude of body and intellect.
Intellect of necessity + ordering of affects + adequate causality → relative freedom as intelligible participation in the nexus of causes.
Adequate Reason → desire for knowledge of the third kind → intuition of singular essence → intellectual Love.
Intuitive knowledge + active joy + intellectual Love → blessedness → increase of intellect → stability of freedom under necessity.
Plurality of affects → reduction to changes of power → asymmetry of causal forces → servitude → rational affect → common composition → adequate intelligence → active blessedness.
Imaginative conflict → coercive State → security → rights and cooperation → citizens' own causality → acquiescence under necessity.
Affective and enduring Body → materially increased aptitude → ordering of images → more actions → intuitive knowledge → greater proportion of Mind understood under eternity.
The psychology of affects is reordered into an ecology of power, where bodies, institutions, and ideas are not separate regions but modes of one causal distribution.
The morality of external acts collapses; value is transferred to the mode of causation, the effect upon the power of the whole, and affective or intellectual origin.
Body and economy are transferred from adjuncts of ethics into constitutive conditions of knowledge, freedom, and rational disposition.
The opposition between the State and freedom is replaced by the opposition between the regime of fear and an order that collectively changes the proportion of action to passion.
Necessity is reclassified from an external limit of agency into the immanent field of relational autonomy and intelligence of causal nexuses.
God and eternity are transferred from persons or temporal continuations to the reflexive structure of immanent causality and the conception of essence under necessity.
A reading of the system must follow the changing functions of terms, because act, affect, Body, freedom, and blessedness preserve nominal identity while changing structural status.
At the surface level, the system treats names of affects, utilities, laws, body, death, and blessedness as questions of human life under servitude and freedom.
At the structural level, all cases are distributed through changes of body, partial causality, social mediation, and the order of ideas.
At the metastrategic level, governance passes from condemnation of passions to production of active affects, cooperation, and cognitive joy.
At the ontological and temporal level, the subject is a necessarily determined part of Nature, whose imaginative duration is distinguished from intelligible eternity.

At the methodological and performative level, demonstration itself performs the reduction, reclassification, and change that it describes, until negation is converted into the positive circuit of blessedness.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Truth has no automatic dominion, yet terminal freedom depends on intelligence; the quantity and form of knowledge that produce sufficient affective force remain undetermined.
Rational concord is said to be necessary, but a State founded on threats cannot derive rational cooperation from security alone.

The Body is temporal and a part of the perishing structure of the Mind, but its aptitude is said to produce greater participation in eternity without full demonstration of the mechanism of proportion.
The negation of finality coheres with the attractor of knowledge of God and blessedness only if the attractor is understood as an immanent cause, not as a preordained end of Nature.
Virtue remains independent of knowledge of eternity, although the highest figure of the wise is defined through eternal intellect and intellectual Love.
Eternal intellectual Love is posited without beginning, but access to intuitive knowledge is narrated in the form of gradually acquired progression.
Desire constitutes a point of mutation where it passes from primitive affect into actual essence, active desire, and the principle of higher knowledge.
The State changes function where it passes from external coercion into a converter of security, cooperation, and the citizens' own causality.
The Body changes function where it passes from the seat of duration and passion into a positive disposition toward action, knowledge, and intelligible eternity.
Necessity changes meaning where it passes from an indicator of external excess into an object of acquiescence and the form of the freedom of the wise.
Blessedness loses terminal status where it is inverted from the end of discipline into virtue itself and the cause of diminishing passions.
Reality is implicitly a network of finite forces, bodies, institutions, and ideas, in which causality is continuously distributed, composed, or captured.
The subject is a permeable, bodily and socially composed node, which becomes free insofar as determining nexuses are more clearly expressed through it.
Time is a bifurcated topology: duration distributes presence, memory, and passion, but eternity displays essence without succession or recollection.
Navigation is possible as a spiral conversion of causal channels: conflict is transferred into cooperation, external fixation into intelligence, and fear of mortality into present blessedness.
The axioms of necessity, affect, conatus, social composition, aptitude of the Body, and intelligence suffice to restore the minimal machine of this level.
The production of a stronger rational affect, the conversion of the coercive State, and the relation of the experience of eternity to the Mind losing memory are not yet sufficiently determined.
The firmest structure is the circuit connecting conatus, cooperation, adequate idea, intellect of necessity, and increased power of knowing.

The reconstruction preserves the true movement if it presents freedom as recursive amplification of power and temporal remedies as a disposition toward intuitive knowledge, not as instantaneous liberation.

At this level the system coheres through the return of terms with altered function, but the nexus between demonstration, the experience of eternity, and the force of the image of the wise resists full reduction.

items.text: Totum systema quaerit quomodo Natura necessario immanens subiecta finita, passionibus et causis externis implicata, libertatem communem atque intellectualem sine exemptione causali generare possit.
Thesis globalis libertatem constituit ut amplificationem causalitatis propriae qua expressio finita Naturae a determinatione partiali ad actionem corpoream, socialem et intellectualem transit.

Argumentatio geometrica simul genealogica, apophatica et reconstructiva fit: exterioritates fictas dissolvit, earum genesim naturalem explicat, deinde functiones ab illis occupatas intra immanentiam restituit.

Motus procedit a causalitate immanenti ad individuationem corpoream, imaginationem et conatum, inde per servitutem affectivam et compositionem civilem ad cognitionem intuitivam atque Amorem intellectualem.
Progressio est cumulativa et spiralis, quia quisque gradus mechanismos priorum retinet sed eorum functionem mutat, atque terminus in condiciones propriae productionis retroagit.
Necessitas ab clausura quae omnem exterioritatem excludit in medium individuationis, interventionis et tandem libertatis sapientis invertitur.
Clausura terminalis non finem remunerativum sed beatitudinem activam producit, quae ex termino apparente in causam permanentem virtutis et intelligentiae convertitur.
Systema immanenter clauditur, sed pons inter cognitionem causalem, transformationem affectuum, cooperationem civilem et stabilitatem beatificam demonstrative incompletus manet.
[Persistent] Una Natura ex necessitate propria existit et agit ut causa immanens omnium rerum; nulla causalitas primaria extra eam stat.
[Persistent] Omne finitum est modus, iar Mens et Corpus sunt expressiones eiusdem individui, non substantiae separatae aut causaliter transversae.
[Mutating] Individuum est relatio corporea perseverans, cuius essentia actualis conatus est et cuius identitas per continuas compositiones conservatur.
[Mutating] Affectio, idea affectionis et variatio potentiae sunt tres functiones unius occursus, qui secundum causalitatem partialem vel adaequatam passionem aut actionem producit.
[Persistent] Adaequatio causalitatem activam designat, inadaequatio autem dependentiam qua effectus singularis tantum partialiter per propriam naturam explicatur.
[Mutating] Imaginatio est mechanismus naturalis praesentificationis et associationis, qui simul capturam affectivam, conservationem conatus et materiam reordinationis rationalis praebet.
[Emergent] Bonum, malum et perfectio sunt indices comparativi relationis inter appetitum, compositionem et potentiam finitam, non proprietates transcendentes rerum.
[Mutating] Subiectum socialiter distribuitur: imitatio affectiva potest conflictum amplificare, sed eadem dependentia per Civitatem et cooperationem in potentiam communem converti potest.
[Terminal] Libertas est gradus causalitatis adaequatae intra necessitatem, non indifferentia, decretum absolutum aut interruptio nexus naturalis.
[Mutating] Cognitio efficax repraesentatio iners esse nequit, sed affectum, ordinem Corporis, institutiones vel facultatem ulterius intelligendi causaliter mutare debet.
[Mutating] Corpus ex obiecto affectionum in infrastructuram materialem libertatis et instrumentum ampliandae potentiae Mentis mutatur.
[Emergent] Civitas est convertor inter servitutem et libertatem quatenus coercitionem et securitatem in iura, cooperationem et maiorem causalitatem civium traducit.
[Emergent] Tempus stratificatur in necessitatem aeternam, durationem conatus, praesentificationem imaginativam et intellectionem essentiae sine successione.
[Attractor] Intelligibilitas causalis, cognitio Dei, acquiescentia et Amor intellectualis constituunt attractorem ascensionalem potentiae activae et non-rivalis.
[Terminal] Beatitudo non est praemium futurum, sed exercitium virtutis quod, ex fine apparente, in machinam sui conservationis convertitur.
Substantia identitatem ontologicam retinet, sed post constitutam immanentiam e proscenio recedit et terminaliter ut ecologia multiscalaris potentiae reapparet.
Necessitas a clausura modalitatis ad genesim passionis, ordinationem affectuum, acquiescentiam et formam libertatis intellectualis migrat.
Corpus a modo determinato in individuum relationale, substratum variationis potentiae, infrastructuram materialem et instrumentum intellectuale transformatur.
Imaginatio ab errore generali in mechanismum neutralem et socialem mutatur, sed sub specie aeternitatis functio eius memorativa terminaliter exhauritur.
Conatus ab essentia perseverandi ad selectionem imaginum, virtutem rationalem, cooperationem communem et actionem intellectualem amplificatur.
Socialitas redit functione mutata: affectus alienus reciprocitatem conflictivam excitat, Civitas eam coercet, iar cooperatio rationalis in amplificationem communem vertit.
Valor ab exemplari externo ad indicem potentiae migrat, deinde ut instrumentum navigationis finitae adhibetur et in beatitudine perfectiore recedit.
Libertas inversionem duplicem patitur: primum indifferentiam amittit, deinde ex causalitate singulari in ecologiam corporalem, civilem atque intellectualem extenditur.
Cognitio Dei ab attractore intellectionis ad Amorem intellectualem progreditur, dum beatitudo statum terminalem amittit et fit causa activa totius progressionis.
Demonstrationes de unicitate substantiae et distinctiones modorum inferiores architecturam praebent; hoc gradu earum functio est clausura exterioritatis per totum campum ethicum servata.
Taxonomiae affectuum et casus actuum inferiores manent; gradus totius libri eos in leges mutationis potentiae, causalitatis et compositionis comprimit.
Vestigia corporalia et concursus imaginum sunt mechanismi locales; sursum fiunt infrastructura qua memoria, expectatio et praesentia affectiva durationem distribuunt.
Aestimatio actuum singularium ex specie externa obsolescit, quia totius libri genealogia valorem ad causam, proportionem actionis et effectum in potentiam transfert.
Parallelismus attributorum ontologiam cum psychologia coniungit, sed manet commissura inferior cuius congruentia positiva ultra identitatem expressionis non explicatur.
Nutritio, labor, lex et Civitas sunt media localia; hoc gradu in condiciones materiales distribuendae causalitatis propriae absorbentur.
Beatitudo, quae in priore structura attractor nondum completus erat, clausuram activam accipit, quamquam nexus affectus rationalis, cooperationis et intuitionis adhuc non plene demonstratur.
Nullus locus extra Naturam admittitur ex quo causae, fines, normae aut libertas originem accipiant.
Nulla actio humana seriem causarum interrumpit; libertas arbitrii et actus incausatus excluduntur.
Mens et Corpus neque substantiae separatae neque adversarii ethici sunt; libertas Mentis per aptitudinem Corporis producitur.
Nullum tribunal morale transcendens aut finis externus ordinem Naturae, valorem rerum vel rectitudinem actionis antecedit.
Subiectum nec sibi transparens nec affective sui iuris nec relationibus externis sufficiens est.
Cognitio causaliter iners passionem superare non potest; contradictio logica sine mutatione affectus et Corporis insufficiens est.
Aeternitas neque continuatio memoriae personalis neque spatium remunerationis post mortem est.
Falsum esse oportet ontologiam, cognitionem, politicam et ethicam ordines causaliter separatos constituere, quia omnes distributiones unius immanentiae sunt.
Falsum esse oportet errorem et passionem irruptiones irrationales extra Naturam esse; eorum ignorantia mechanismis corporalibus, imaginativis et socialibus stabilitur.
Falsum esse oportet dependentiam finiti meram privationem esse, quia eadem relatio quae servitutem permittit mutuum auxilium et potentiam communem generat.
Falsum esse oportet speciem exteriorem actus eius valorem continere, cum idem opus passionem, rationem vel virtutem exprimere possit.
Falsum esse oportet coercitionem et securitatem per se cooperationem rationalem efficere; regimen metus circuitum servitutis recreare potest.
Falsum esse oportet beatitudinem mercedem futuram aut virtutem calculatione praemii sustentatam esse.
Absentia suprema est exterioritas absoluta, locus unde Naturae totalitas sine participatione causali spectari aut gubernari posset.
Origo absoluta cogitationis, appetitus vel actionis ontologice indisponibilis est; omne initium nexus iam constituti modulatio est.
Praesentia immediata rei aut sui, corporali et historica mediatione carens, excluditur una cum prospectu causas totius sine participatione cognoscente.
Systema circum impossibilitatem liberationis instantaneae et absolutae ordinatur: veritas non statim fit potentia, iar homo finitus numquam omnibus causis externis vacat.
Quia ontologia iam veritatem et actionem ut gradus unius integrationis causalis constituit, remedia ethica non secundum imperium additum sed secundum redistributionem eiusdem causalitatis operantur.
Cum imaginatio simul capturam et conservationem sustineat, veritas vim practicam obtinet tantum ubi imagines, affectus et dispositiones corporales ab intra reordinat.
Individuum relationale et subiectum metastabile efficiunt ut libertas sit ecologia distributa corporis, societatis et intellectus, non possessio subiecti clausi.
Normativitas est cartographia temporaria compositionum: bonum et malum necessaria sunt navigationi finitae, sed opere beatitudinis peracto functionem amittunt.
Politica est conversio circuituum affectivorum, qua circulatio imaginum et attributionum ex reciprocitate conflictiva in cooperationem potentiam amplificantem traducitur.
Praxis ethica non in tempore uno progreditur, sed praesentiam imaginativam, durationem deliberativam et aeternitatem intelligibilem sine earum reductione coordinat.
Generositas et Amor intellectualis sunt duae scalae potentiae non-rivalis, quarum prima relationes humanas componit et altera ipsam immanentiam reflexive intelligit.
Transitus a cognitione ad stabilitatem affectivam requirit affectum rationalem, Civitatem cooperativam et dispositionem corporalem, sed nexus causaliter sufficiens horum mediorum incompletus manet.
Realitas fit ecologia sui modulationis, in qua substantia, corpora, affectus, institutiones et ideae sunt altitudines unius causalitatis immanentis.
Subiectum est proportio multiscalaris causalitatum, cuius agentia crescit vel decrescit secundum modum quo nexus determinantes per ipsum exprimuntur.
Epistemologia fit technologia causalis, quia intelligere significat condiciones compositionis, affectionis et ulterioris cognitionis reordinare.
Politica fit distributio condicionum causalitatis propriae, non administratio voluntatum iam formatarum aut mera suppressio conflictus.
Ethica est conversio capturarum necessariarum in compositiones non-rivales, qua finitas non tollitur sed potentiam cognoscendi et agendi auget.
Historia subiecti non in tempore homogeno continetur, sed ex coordinatione durationis, praesentificationis, deliberationis et intellectionis aeternae constat.
Methodus geometrica performative naturalizat: negationes transcendentes in geneses causales resolvit et geneses in circuitus positivos libertatis convertit.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Immanentia psychologiam naturalizat; psychologia fictionem exterioritatis explicat; explicata exterioritas vicissim clausuram immanentiae confirmat.
Affectio imaginem generat, imago Cupiditatem dirigit, Cupiditas corpus et relationes mutat, iar mutatum corpus novas affectiones sub alia proportione recipit.
Adaequatio actionem auget, actio clariorem causae intellectionem firmat, iar claritas aucta ulteriorem passivitatem minuit.
Affectus reciprocus conflictum amplificat; coercitio securitatem inducere potest, sed circuitus ad servitutem regreditur si metus fundamentum institutionis manet.
Convenientia rationalis cooperationem auget, cooperatio potentiam singularem amplificat, iar potentia aucta maiorem communicationem boni non-rivalis efficit.
Oeconomia Corporis libertatem cognitionis sustinet, cognitio aptitudinem agendi auget, iar corpus aptius plures ideas adaequatas recipit.
Causalitas adaequata est attractor medius, beatitudo attractor terminalis; prior transitum ordinat, altera transitum in circuitum sui conservationis claudit.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Natura necessario existens → exclusio exterioritatis → causalitas immanens → modi finiti causaliter dependentes.
Modus finitus → individuum corporeum relationale → idem processus sub Cogitatione et Extensione → Mens ut idea Corporis.
Occursus corporalis → affectio → idea affectionis → vestigium et praesentificatio → imaginatio perspectivalis.
Conatus → Cupiditas → mutatio potentiae → Laetitia aut Tristitia → actio vel passio secundum adaequationem causae.
Imaginatio alterius → imitatio affectus → reciprocitas → conflictus, rivalitas aut compositio socialis.
Affectus contrarius + aptitudo Corporis + convenientia rationalis + auxilia communia → maior causalitas propria.
Ratio adaequata → cupiditas cognitionis tertii generis → intuitio essentiae singularis → Amor intellectualis.
Amor intellectualis + laetitia activa → beatitudo → augmentum intellectus → imminutio passionum → stabilitas libertatis.
Immanentia → individuum corporeum → Mens → affectio → imaginatio → conatus → mutatio potentiae → servitus affectiva.
Ignorantia causarum → fines et valores proiecti → fixatio causae externae → imminutio potentiae → ulterior ignorantia.
Imitatio conflictiva → Civitas coercitiva → securitas → convenientia rationalis → cooperatio → potentia communis.
Cognitio causalis → affectus activus → causalitas propria → intuitio → Amor intellectualis → beatitudo ut exercitium virtutis.
Oppositio Dei et mundi corruit, iar theologia in ontologiam reflexivam causalitatis immanentis convertitur.
Oppositio Mentis et Corporis cedit duplici expressioni unius individui, cuius oeconomia corporea cognitionem constitutive condicionat.
Cognitio et agentia in unam scalam causalitatis coalescunt, unde epistemologia statum technologiae transformationis accipit.
Moralitas actuum exteriorum corruit, iar valor fit index causae, compositionis et mutationis potentiae.
Socialitas non iam aggregatio subiectorum praeconstitutorum est, iar Civitas non opponitur libertati nisi regimen metus causalitatem civium minuit.
Tempus reclassificatur a successione homogena in pluralitatem durationis, praesentiae affectivae et aeternitatis intelligibilis.
Interventio transit ab imperio et iudicio ad analysin geneticam, iar lectio debet mutationes functionales terminorum potius quam identitatem nominalem sequi.
In gradu superficiei Deus, Natura, Mens, Corpus, affectus, lex, mors et beatitudo sunt obiecta declarata per quae quaestio servitutis et libertatis tractatur.
In gradu structurali obiecta distribuuntur per causalitatem immanentem, individuationem relationalem, mediationem socialem, conatum et proportiones causae partialis vel adaequatae.
In gradu metastrategico quaestio ab electione et condemnatione ad generationem affectuum activorum, compositionem potentiae et condiciones interventionis transfertur.
In gradu ontologico et temporali realitas est productio necessaria, subiectum pars relationalis Naturae, iar duratio imaginativa ab aeternitate intelligibili distinguitur.
In gradu methodologico et performativo deductio genetica exterioritates dissolvit et negationem ipsam in circuitum positivum libertatis convertit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Attributa per se concipiuntur, sed earum distinctio cum unitate substantiae per exclusionem pluralitatis potius quam per coordinationem positivam stabilitur.
Causalitas divina omnes modos determinat, sed mediatio inter productivitatem aeternam et series finitas immediate causantes nimis compressa manet.
Parallelismus identitatem processus Mentis et Corporis servat, sed principium positivum congruentiae ultra duplicem expressionem non explicat.
Falsitas privatio cognitionis dicitur, quamquam condiciones erroris positive producuntur; statutum normativum et genesis causalis eodem vocabulo non plene reconciliantur.
Veritas imperium automaticum non habet, sed libertas terminalis ab intelligentia pendet; limen quo intellecta necessitas vim affectivam sufficientem acquirit indeterminatum manet.
Concordia rationalis finem politicum ordinat, sed Civitas metu fundata cooperationem ex securitate sola deducere nequit.
Corpus temporale maiorem participationem intellectionis aeternae parare dicitur, sed proportio inter aptitudinem corporalem et aeternitatem Mentis non plene demonstratur.
Negatio finalitatis cum attractore beatitudinis cohaeret tantum si beatitudo causa immanens progressionis, non finis Naturae praestitutus, intelligitur.
Necessitas punctum mutationis attingit ubi ex clausura contingentiae et signo dominationis in obiectum acquiescentiae atque formam libertatis transit.
Imaginatio punctum mutationis attingit ubi ex praeiudicio fit mechanismus neutralis et conservativus, deinde sub aeternitate operationem memorativam amittit.
Corpus punctum mutationis attingit ubi ex obiecto Mentis et sede passionis in dispositionem positivam ad actionem, cognitionem et intellectum aeternitatis transit.
Adaequatio punctum mutationis attingit ubi ex qualitate veritatis in affectum activum et causalitatem transformativam convertitur.
Civitas punctum mutationis attingit ubi exterior coercitio in securitatem, cooperationem et causalitatem propriam civium convertitur.
Beatitudo punctum mutationis terminale constituit ubi statum finis amittit et fit exercitium virtutis atque causa conservandae libertatis.
Realitas est machina immanens et rete virium, in quo causalitas non exit ex Natura sed inter corpora, institutiones et ideas perpetuo redistribuitur.
Subiectum est vortex corporeus et nodus permeabilis, cuius autonomia non clausura sed clarior expressio nexuum per ipsum agentium est.
Tempus est machina stratificata et topologia bifurcata, in qua duratio mutationes memorativas distribuit, aeternitas autem essentiam sine successione exhibet.
Captura est circuitus quo causa externa potentiam minuit, ignorantiam stabilit et speciem libertatis sub ipsa dependentia producit.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga e machina, sed conversio spiralis canalium causalium qua conflictus, fixatio externa et metus in cooperationem, intelligentiam et beatitudinem transferuntur.
Axiomata immanentiae, individuationis corporeae, conatus, imaginationis, adaequationis, compositionis socialis et beatitudinis activae sufficiunt ad machinam minimam totius libri restituendam.
Structura firmissima est circuitus continuus quo causalitas immanens affectionem, affectio potentiam, cooperatio adaequationem et adaequatio ulteriorem potentiam cognoscendi generat.
Minus determinata manet productio affectus rationalis fortioris, conversio Civitatis coercitivae et nexus inter aptitudinem Corporis, intuitionem atque experientiam aeternitatis.
Systema hac magnitudine cohaeret si non ut series doctrinarum sed ut circuitus a metaphysica ad corpus, ab imaginatione ad servitutem et a servitute ad beatitudinem legitur.
Restitutio motum generativum servat, sed singularitas affectuum, differentiae corporum et vis performativa imaginis sapientis reductioni axiomaticae plenae resistunt.
The whole system asks how finite subjects necessarily immanent in Nature, implicated in passions and external causes, can generate common and intellectual freedom without causal exemption.

The global thesis establishes freedom as the amplification of one's own causality through which a finite expression of Nature passes from partial determination to bodily, social, and intellectual action.

The geometrical argumentation becomes at once genealogical, apophatic, and reconstructive: it dissolves fictitious exteriorities, explains their natural genesis, then restores within immanence the functions occupied by them.
The movement proceeds from immanent causality to bodily individuation, imagination, and conatus, thence through affective servitude and civil composition to intuitive knowledge and intellectual Love.

The progression is cumulative and spiral, because each stage retains the mechanisms of the preceding ones but changes their function, and the terminus acts back upon the conditions of its own production.
Necessity is inverted from a closure excluding all exteriority into a medium of individuation, intervention, and finally wise freedom.
Terminal closure produces not a remunerative end but active blessedness, which is converted from an apparent terminus into a permanent cause of virtue and intelligence.
The system closes immanently, but the bridge between causal knowledge, transformation of the affects, civil cooperation, and beatific stability remains demonstratively incomplete.
[Persistent] One Nature exists and acts from its own necessity as the immanent cause of all things; no primary causality stands outside it.
[Persistent] Everything finite is a mode, and Mind and Body are expressions of the same individual, not separate or causally transverse substances.
[Mutating] The individual is a persisting bodily relation, whose actual essence is conatus and whose identity is preserved through continuous compositions.
[Mutating] An affection, the idea of an affection, and a variation of power are three functions of one occurrence, which according to partial or adequate causality produces passion or action.
[Persistent] Adequacy designates active causality, whereas inadequacy designates the dependence by which a singular effect is only partially explained through its own nature.
[Mutating] Imagination is a natural mechanism of making-present and association, which simultaneously provides affective capture, preservation of conatus, and material for rational reordering.
[Emergent] Good, evil, and perfection are comparative indices of the relation between appetite, composition, and finite power, not transcendent properties of things.
[Mutating] The subject is socially distributed: affective imitation can amplify conflict, but the same dependence can be converted through the State and cooperation into common power.
[Terminal] Freedom is a degree of adequate causality within necessity, not indifference, absolute decree, or interruption of the natural nexus.
[Mutating] Effective knowledge cannot be inert representation, but must causally alter affect, the order of the Body, institutions, or the capacity to understand further.
[Mutating] The Body is transformed from an object of affections into the material infrastructure of freedom and an instrument for amplifying the power of the Mind.
[Emergent] The State is a converter between servitude and freedom insofar as it translates coercion and security into rights, cooperation, and the greater causality of citizens.
[Emergent] Time is stratified into eternal necessity, the duration of conatus, imaginative making-present, and the understanding of essence without succession.
[Attractor] Causal intelligibility, knowledge of God, acquiescence, and intellectual Love constitute an ascending attractor of active and non-rivalrous power.
[Terminal] Blessedness is not a future reward, but an exercise of virtue which, from an apparent end, is converted into a mechanism of its own preservation.
Substance retains its ontological identity, but after immanence has been established it recedes from the foreground and terminally reappears as a multiscalar ecology of power.
Necessity migrates from the closure of modality to the genesis of passion, the ordering of affects, acquiescence, and the form of intellectual freedom.
The Body is transformed from a determined mode into a relational individual, a substrate of variation in power, material infrastructure, and an intellectual instrument.
Imagination changes from a general error into a neutral and social mechanism, but under the aspect of eternity its memorial function is terminally exhausted.
Conatus is amplified from the essence of persevering into the selection of images, rational virtue, common cooperation, and intellectual action.
Sociality returns with altered function: another's affect excites conflictual reciprocity, the State restrains it, and rational cooperation converts it into common amplification.
Value migrates from an external model to an index of power, is then used as an instrument of finite navigation, and recedes in more perfect blessedness.
Freedom undergoes a double inversion: first it loses indifference, then it extends from singular causality into a bodily, civil, and intellectual ecology.
Knowledge of God advances from the attractor of understanding to intellectual Love, while blessedness loses its terminal status and becomes the active cause of the whole progression.

Demonstrations of the uniqueness of substance and distinctions of modes provide the lower architecture; at this level their function is the closure of exteriority maintained throughout the whole ethical field.
Taxonomies of affects and cases of actions remain lower; the level of the whole book compresses them into laws of the mutation of power, causality, and composition.
Bodily traces and the concurrence of images are local mechanisms; at a higher level they become the infrastructure through which memory, expectation, and affective presence distribute duration.
The evaluation of singular acts from their external appearance becomes obsolete, because the genealogy of the whole book transfers value to cause, the proportion of action, and the effect upon power.
The parallelism of attributes joins ontology to psychology, but remains a lower joint whose positive congruence beyond identity of expression is not explained.
Nutrition, labor, law, and the State are local media; at this level they are absorbed into the material conditions for distributing one's own causality.

Blessedness, which in the prior structure was an attractor not yet complete, receives active closure, although the nexus of rational affect, cooperation, and intuition is still not fully demonstrated.
No place outside Nature is admitted from which causes, ends, norms, or freedom might receive their origin.
No human action interrupts the series of causes; freedom of the will and uncaused act are excluded.
Mind and Body are neither separate substances nor ethical adversaries; the freedom of the Mind is produced through the aptitude of the Body.
No transcendent moral tribunal or external end precedes the order of Nature, the value of things, or the rectitude of action.
The subject is neither transparent to itself, nor affectively self-governing, nor sufficient unto itself in relation to external relations.
Causally inert knowledge cannot overcome passion; logical contradiction without a change in affect and Body is insufficient.
Eternity is neither the continuation of personal memory nor a space of remuneration after death.
It must be false that ontology, knowledge, politics, and ethics constitute causally separate orders, because they are all distributions of one immanence.
It must be false that error and passion are irrational irruptions outside Nature; their ignorance is stabilized by bodily, imaginative, and social mechanisms.
It must be false that the dependence of the finite is mere privation, because the same relation that permits servitude generates mutual aid and common power.
It must be false that the external appearance of an act contains its value, since the same deed can express passion, reason, or virtue.
It must be false that coercion and security by themselves effect rational cooperation; a regime of fear can recreate the circuit of servitude.
It must be false that blessedness is a future recompense or that virtue is sustained by calculation of reward.
The supreme absence is absolute exteriority, a place from which the totality of Nature could be contemplated or governed without causal participation.
An absolute origin of thought, appetite, or action is ontologically unavailable; every beginning is a modulation of an already established nexus.
Immediate presence of a thing or of oneself, lacking bodily and historical mediation, is excluded together with the prospect of knowing the causes of the whole without participation.
The system is ordered around the impossibility of instantaneous and absolute liberation: truth does not immediately become power, and the finite human being is never free of all external causes.

Because ontology already constitutes truth and action as degrees of one causal integration, ethical remedies operate not according to an added command but according to a redistribution of the same causality.
Since imagination simultaneously sustains capture and preservation, truth obtains practical force only where it reorders images, affects, and bodily dispositions from within.
The relational individual and the metastable subject entail that freedom is a distributed ecology of body, society, and intellect, not the possession of a closed subject.
Normativity is a temporary cartography of compositions: good and evil are necessary for finite navigation, but lose their function once the work of blessedness has been accomplished.
Politics is the conversion of affective circuits, through which the circulation of images and attributions is translated from conflictual reciprocity into power-amplifying cooperation.
Ethical praxis does not progress in a single time, but coordinates imaginative presence, deliberative duration, and intelligible eternity without reducing them.
Generosity and intellectual Love are two scales of non-rivalrous power, the former composing human relations and the latter reflexively understanding immanence itself.
The transition from knowledge to affective stability requires rational affect, a cooperative State, and bodily disposition, but the causally sufficient nexus of these means remains incomplete.
Reality becomes an ecology of self-modulation, in which substance, bodies, affects, institutions, and ideas are levels of one immanent causality.
The subject is a multiscalar proportion of causalities, whose agency increases or decreases according to the manner in which determining nexuses are expressed through it.
Epistemology becomes causal technology, because to understand means to reorder the conditions of composition, affection, and further knowledge.
Politics becomes the distribution of the conditions of one's own causality, not the administration of already formed wills or the mere suppression of conflict.
Ethics is the conversion of necessary captures into non-rivalrous compositions, through which finitude is not removed but the power of knowing and acting is increased.
The history of the subject is not contained in homogeneous time, but consists in the coordination of duration, making-present, deliberation, and eternal understanding.
The geometrical method naturalizes performatively: it resolves transcendent negations into causal geneses and converts geneses into positive circuits of freedom.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Immanence naturalizes psychology; psychology explains the fiction of exteriority; explained exteriority in turn confirms the closure of immanence.
Affection generates an image, the image directs Desire, Desire changes the body and relations, and the changed body receives new affections under another proportion.
Adequacy increases action, action confirms a clearer understanding of the cause, and increased clarity diminishes further passivity.
Reciprocal affect amplifies conflict; coercion can induce security, but the circuit regresses into servitude if fear remains the foundation of the institution.
Rational agreement increases cooperation, cooperation amplifies singular power, and increased power effects greater communication of non-rivalrous good.
The economy of the Body sustains freedom of knowledge, knowledge increases the aptitude for acting, and a more apt body receives more adequate ideas.
Adequate causality is the intermediate attractor, blessedness the terminal attractor; the former orders the transition, the latter closes the transition into a circuit of self-preservation.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessarily existing Nature → exclusion of exteriority → immanent causality → causally dependent finite modes.
Finite mode → relational bodily individual → same process under Thought and Extension → Mind as idea of the Body.
Bodily occurrence → affection → idea of affection → trace and making-present → perspectival imagination.
Conatus → Desire → variation of power → Joy or Sadness → action or passion according to adequacy of cause.
Imagination of another → imitation of affect → reciprocity → conflict, rivalry, or social composition.
Contrary affect + aptitude of the Body + rational agreement + common aids → greater causality of one's own.
Adequate reason → desire for knowledge of the third kind → intuition of singular essence → intellectual Love.
Intellectual Love + active joy → blessedness → increase of intellect → diminution of passions → stability of freedom.
Immanence → bodily individual → Mind → affection → imagination → conatus → variation of power → affective servitude.
Ignorance of causes → projected ends and values → fixation upon an external cause → diminution of power → further ignorance.
Conflictual imitation → coercive State → security → rational agreement → cooperation → common power.
Causal knowledge → active affect → one's own causality → intuition → intellectual Love → blessedness as exercise of virtue.
The opposition of God and world collapses, and theology is converted into a reflexive ontology of immanent causality.
The opposition of Mind and Body gives way to the double expression of one individual, whose bodily economy constitutively conditions knowledge.
Knowledge and agency coalesce into one scale of causality, whence epistemology assumes the status of a technology of transformation.
The morality of external acts collapses, and value becomes an index of cause, composition, and variation of power.
Sociality is no longer an aggregation of preconstituted subjects, and the State is not opposed to freedom unless a regime of fear diminishes the causality of citizens.
Time is reclassified from homogeneous succession into a plurality of duration, affective presence, and intelligible eternity.
Intervention passes from command and judgment to genetic analysis, and reading must follow the functional mutations of terms rather than nominal identity.
At the level of the surface, God, Nature, Mind, Body, affects, law, death, and blessedness are declared objects through which the question of servitude and freedom is treated.
At the structural level, objects are distributed through immanent causality, relational individuation, social mediation, conatus, and the proportions of partial or adequate cause.
At the metastrategic level, the question is transferred from choice and condemnation to the generation of active affects, the composition of power, and the conditions of intervention.
At the ontological and temporal level, reality is necessary production, the subject a relational part of Nature, and imaginative duration is distinguished from intelligible eternity.
At the methodological and performative level, genetic deduction dissolves exteriorities and converts negation itself into a positive circuit of freedom.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Attributes are conceived through themselves, but their distinction from the unity of substance is stabilized through exclusion of plurality rather than through positive coordination.
Divine causality determines all modes, but the mediation between eternal productivity and immediately causing finite series remains overly compressed.
Parallelism preserves the identity of the process of Mind and Body, but does not explain a positive principle of congruence beyond double expression.
Falsity is said to be a privation of knowledge, although the conditions of error are positively produced; normative status and causal genesis are not fully reconciled in the same term.
Truth has no automatic command, but terminal freedom depends on intelligence; the threshold at which understood necessity acquires sufficient affective force remains indeterminate.
Rational concord orders the political end, but a State founded on fear cannot derive cooperation from security alone.
The temporal Body is said to prepare greater participation in eternal understanding, but the proportion between bodily aptitude and the eternity of the Mind is not fully demonstrated.
The negation of finality coheres with the attractor of blessedness only if blessedness is understood as the immanent cause of progression, not as a preordained end of Nature.
Necessity reaches a point of mutation where it passes from the closure of contingency and a sign of domination into an object of acquiescence and a form of freedom.
Imagination reaches a point of mutation where it changes from prejudice into a neutral and preservative mechanism, then under eternity loses its memorial operation.
The Body reaches a point of mutation where it passes from an object of the Mind and seat of passion into a positive disposition for action, knowledge, and understanding of eternity.
Adequacy reaches a point of mutation where it is converted from a quality of truth into active affect and transformative causality.
The State reaches a point of mutation where external coercion is converted into security, cooperation, and the citizens' own causality.
Blessedness constitutes the terminal point of mutation where it loses the status of an end and becomes an exercise of virtue and cause of preserving freedom.
Reality is an immanent machine and network of forces, in which causality does not exit Nature but is perpetually redistributed among bodies, institutions, and ideas.
The subject is a bodily vortex and permeable node, whose autonomy is not closure but a clearer expression of the nexuses acting through it.
Time is a stratified machine and bifurcated topology, in which duration distributes memorial changes, whereas eternity presents essence without succession.
Capture is a circuit through which an external cause diminishes power, stabilizes ignorance, and produces the appearance of freedom under dependence itself.

Possible navigation is not flight from the machine, but the spiral conversion of causal channels through which conflict, external fixation, and fear are transferred into cooperation, intelligence, and blessedness.
The axioms of immanence, bodily individuation, conatus, imagination, adequacy, social composition, and active blessedness suffice to reconstruct the minimal machine of the whole book.
The firmest structure is the continuous circuit through which immanent causality generates affection, affection power, cooperation adequacy, and adequacy a further power of knowing.
Less determined remain the production of a stronger rational affect, the conversion of the coercive State, and the nexus between the aptitude of the Body, intuition, and the experience of eternity.
The system coheres at this magnitude if it is read not as a series of doctrines but as a circuit from metaphysics to body, from imagination to servitude, and from servitude to blessedness.

The reconstruction preserves the generative movement, but the singularity of affects, the differences of bodies, and the performative force of the image of the wise person resist complete axiomatic reduction.
